title: Calf Scramble by Libby Carr at Primary Stages #calfscramble #primarys...
transcript: I just learned what a calf scramble is, and Texas and New York are truly different worlds. Basically, it's a competition where teenagers hand-wrangle calves in an arena with hopes of claiming one that they can subsequently raise for the following year's livestock show. A fierce competition with prize money on the line, plus a healthy dose of teenage angst and uncertainty, makes a great recipe for a play. As five girls raise calves and barrel toward their prospective futures that fill them with excitement and terror, they navigate various revelations and disagreements over faith, love, and responsibility. Despite a relatively slow start, the play has lovely character development and covers a lot of ground in just 90 minutes. The performances are wonderful with some interesting and unexpected physicality, as the actors occasionally embody the cows they're raising — a choice that I haven't decided whether it's innovative and comedic, or jarring and uncomfortable. In any case, I enjoyed the play. With that, another program for my collection.
